# #1572: Patch: the fuzz wave plays the endings and server actions it never submits
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
The randomized-game gate has never once conceded, offered or answered a draw, emoted, timed out a turn, expired a disconnect, or hit the ceiling inside a fuzzed game — those endings and cleanups are covered only by hand-written tests, never across thousands of random boards. After this, a fuzz wave takes them at a low seeded rate, so whole-game random coverage finally reaches the ways a real game can end.

## Why
`play_game` drives `subsystems::choose_action`, which samples `legal_actions` minus `AI_SKIPPED_ACTIONS` — Concede, OfferDraw, AnswerDraw and Emote are always filtered (`crates/engine/src/subsystems/ai_policy.rs:29-37`, `crates/tools/src/fuzz.rs:671-736`). That is correct for §10.7's random policy, but it means the draw-offer state machine (offer once per turn, decline blocks re-offers, lapse at turn end, standing offer in views — `crates/engine/src/turn.rs`, `reduce.rs:870-901`), concede-during-prompt cleanup, and the emote record get zero whole-game randomized coverage. The server-only actions — `timeout` (which resolves open prompts by policy and keeps mulligans whole, R268/R1002/R1184001), `disconnectExpired`, `ceilingReached`, `setAutoEndTurn` (`reduce.rs:287-465`) — likewise never appear; `duos_fuzz.rs` filters Concede too. A drift in draw bookkeeping (stale `drawOffer`, double offers, offers surviving the turn boundary) or a timeout resolving a prompt wrongly would land silently.

## Proposal
Add a seeded endings channel inside `play_game`: a small per-step probability of picking a listed concede/draw/emote action when offered, and a per-seed schedule that forges `timeout`/`setAutoEndTurn` (and near the cap, `ceilingReached`) through the existing probe seam, logged like any action so replays fold them. Keep the rate low enough that games still reach depth; mirror concede/timeout in `duos_fuzz`.

## Where it lands
`crates/tools/src/fuzz.rs`, `crates/tools/src/duos_fuzz.rs`; spec §10.7, the draw rules in `crates/engine/src/turn.rs`, the server actions in `crates/engine/src/reduce.rs`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A fixed-seed fuzz test asserts its log contains concede/draw/emote/timeout actions, so the channel cannot silently regress
- [ ] Replay-fold and state-hash checks still pass on games that end by concede or accepted draw
- [ ] Failures keep naming their seed and decks

## Size and risks
Medium; the risk is tuning the rate so endings don't crowd out normal play — make it small and seeded, and it is one more wave beside the existing ones, not a change to the shipped §10.7 policy.
